# W30 Interaction: Real Claude Code Terminal in the Page

See [[Task Board]] for tasks; contracts are in [[Contracts]] section 14 (7.2, 7.3, 7.4, sections 11 and 13); requirements are in [[Requirements Log]] Round 7, items 1–10. Branch `wfd-w30`, based on main `c747501`.

## Step 1: Live Test

The script is at `server/.work/w30/` (gitignored): `pty-exp.ts` uses node-pty to launch the interactive `claude` (the baseline variant's `runtimeEnv`, `--settings <hooks.json>`), writes keystrokes according to the step file, waits for hooks, and uses `@xterm/headless` to read screen snapshots. The step file, each run's snapshots, `hooks.jsonl`, and `pty.log` are in `.work/w30/exp/`. Claude Code 2.1.295.

### 1. node-pty launches claude, xterm.js displays and takes input over WebSocket — feasible

- The darwin prebuild of `node-pty@1.1.0` (the latest stable release on npm) has no execute permission on `spawn-helper`, so `pty.spawn` directly reports `Error: posix_spawnp failed.`; the `spawn-helper` of `1.2.0-beta.15` is `-rwxr-xr-x`, and startup works normally (`Hello pty\r\n`, `exit { exitCode: 0 }`). Dependencies use `1.2.0-beta.15`, and `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` allows its install script (it only checks the prebuild inside the package and does not compile locally).
- The xterm.js on the page, via `/api/live/:id/pty`, shows Claude Code's startup screen, Chinese conversation and AskUserQuestion menu; keyboard input (↓) moves the menu cursor; after closing the page and reopening it, the terminal first receives the retained output (screenshot `.work/w30/exp/pw-open.png`).
- Claude Code has enabled bracketed paste (`\e[?2004h`), mouse reporting (`\e[?1000h`, `1002h`, `1003h`, `1006h`) and focus events (`\e[?1004h`).

### 2. Hooks from `--settings <hooks.json>` fire in interactive mode - feasible

Observed stdin fields (`.work/w30/exp/basic2-out/hooks.jsonl`, `ask1-out/hooks.jsonl`, `resume-b-out/hooks.jsonl`):

| hook | fields |
|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `source` (`startup` / `resume`), `model`; on resume also `seconds_since_last_response`, `context_tokens` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `prompt_id`, `permission_mode`, `prompt` (the submitted original text) |
| `PreToolUse` (matcher `AskUserQuestion`) | `tool_name: "AskUserQuestion"`, `tool_input.questions` (`question`, `header`, `options[{label, description}]`, `multiSelect`), `tool_use_id` |
| `Stop` | `last_assistant_message` (the last text block of this turn), `background_tasks` (array; when non-empty, Claude Code starts the next turn by itself), `stop_hook_active`, `effort` |
| `Notification` | once when waiting for input and once when the menu appears |

- The variant's own hooks (wf's SessionStart, Stop, etc.) keep running as usual; the hooks from `--settings` coexist with them.
- Two screens appear before any hook and have no hooks: the working-directory trust dialog (Is this a project you trust?), and the first-run onboarding when the config directory is first launched interactively (pick a theme, security notes). For the orchestrator's handling, see "Key decisions".

### 3. Answering AskUserQuestion by writing keystrokes to the PTY - feasible

Observed (`ask1` … `ask6`; per-step screen snapshots are in `.work/w30/exp/ask*-out/`):

| case | keys | result |
|---|---|---|
| Single choice, pick item n | digit `n` | selects it and moves to the next question (when the cursor is on "Type something", the digit is typed into the input box) |
| Single choice "Other" | move the cursor to "Type something" (line `k+1`), type the text, `\r` | the answer is the typed text |
| Multi-select | digit toggles the checkbox (cursor stays put); or move the cursor to that line and `\r` to toggle | `[✔]` |
| Multi-select "Other" | cursor `↓` to "Type something", type the text (auto-checked) | answer is a label plus text, like `apple, plus watermelon` |
| Multi-select, go to next question | `↓` to the `Next` / `Submit` line, `\r`; or `→` | next question or Review |
| Multiple questions, or the only question is multi-select | the Review page appears last, `1` (Submit answers) | submits; a single-select as the only question submits as soon as it is selected, with no Review |
| `↑` on item 1 | wraps to the last item (cycles) | the cursor position cannot be inferred from relative moves |
| Text answer | `\e[200~…\e[201~` (paste), then write `\r` separately | multi-line text is submitted as one message |

Because `↑` cycles, digits typed into the input box are treated as text, and a person may have moved the cursor or ticked boxes before handing back, the implementation does not use a fixed key sequence: the dashboard keeps a copy of the screen on the server using `@xterm/headless`, reads the current question's menu before answering (the question text follows directly after the last-line tab bar `☐/☒ header`, and after that come the numbered options and `Next/Submit`), presses keys step by step according to the cursor line and checked state, and waits for the screen to change after each press (`server/src/live/keys.ts`'s `readMenu`, `answerMenu`).

### 4. resume - feasible

- After copying the session's jsonl into another `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (`cfg2/projects/live-b/`), `claude --resume <id>` continues the conversation ("For the color question you picked "other" and typed "purple, a bit grey""), the session id is unchanged, it keeps writing to the copied file, and the original file's sha is unchanged.
- Where Claude Code looks: `--resume <id>` searches all subdirectories of `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/` for `<id>.jsonl` and keeps writing to the one it finds (without `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` it still finds the one in `live-b/`). With `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=<subdirectory name>` set, the `transcript_path` in `SessionStart` also points to this file; without it, `SessionStart` reports the path of the cwd slug directory, and the later hooks give the actual file. The implementation copies to `projects/<liveId>/` and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` to the name of the subdirectory containing the file.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` also works in interactive mode: a new interactive session writes to `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<liveId>/<sessionId>.jsonl`.

## What was done

| part | file |
|---|---|
| Data: `live_sessions`, `live_events`, `sessions.live_id`; migration `0006_live_sessions.sql` (only adds tables and columns) | `server/src/db/schema.ts`, `server/drizzle/` |
| Launch: isolated (lfg `createEmptyRunRepo`, ic `createRunRepo` + `createRunTicket`, `gh repo clone` into `data/live/<liveId>/workspace`, sandbox same as run, `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED=1`, `MAGI_VAULT`, lfg's `MAGI_PRODUCT`, initial message same as run); real (the real directory must exist; lfg `/lfg <idea>`, ic `/ic <ticket number>`); arguments are the variant's `--model --effort --mcp-config`, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, `--settings data/live/<liveId>/hooks.json`, `--session-id` and the initial message; hooks.json contains `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` and five hooks, with the command `curl … --data-binary @- '<service address>/api/live/<id>/hook'` | `server/src/live/index.ts` |
| PTY: node-pty, the most recent 4 MB of output kept in memory (discarded in whole chunks), full output written to `pty.log`, server-side headless screen copy | `server/src/live/pty.ts` |
| Hook-driven state and simulated-user driving: `Stop` (when there are no background tasks) and AskUserQuestion's `PreToolUse` set to waiting; `UserPromptSubmit` clears it; on resume, `SessionStart` waits for the previous turn's text; before the first `SessionStart` is received, the driver is fixed as human. The simulated user reuses `runs/simulated-user.ts`: text answers are pasted and then Enter is sent; option answers are pressed on screen by `answerMenu`. Client key presses (except mouse reporting and focus events) switch the driver to human; an answer being generated is cancelled via AbortController and recorded as void; when handing back, AskUserQuestion items that already have a result (read from the jsonl) are not answered again; when `done` or the number of answers reaches `maxUserTurns`, control goes to the human; errors from the simulated user and from import are written to `error` and control goes to the human | `server/src/live/controller.ts`, `server/src/live/keys.ts` |
| The simulated user's context changes to `{ task: { kind, persona, hiddenRequirements }, eval: { runId, repo, ticket, product } \| null, signal }`: run passes the task and the eval environment; when a task is selected during interaction, use that task; for on-the-spot input, persona is "the person who proposed this idea (or ticket)..."; in the real environment there are no eval environment facts and no authorization notes (only operations necessary to complete this work are authorized); when the resume session comes from a run, use the run's task. Answers additionally carry `selections` (option number and "other") | `server/src/runs/simulated-user.ts`, `server/src/runs/runner.ts` |
| resume: environment fixed to real, cwd is the working directory recorded in the session; when the projects of the target config (the variant's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or the "local config"'s `<HOME>/.claude` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` left unset) do not contain this session, first import the original file, then copy the jsonl and the same-named directory (subagents, tool-results) to `projects/<liveId>/`; change `sessions.file_path` and the subagent paths to the copied ones, and point `sessions.live_id` to this interaction; the original file is not imported afterwards (`ingestFile` does not error or import when it encounters an original file that was resumed elsewhere); the default variant is the variant used by the run or interaction | `server/src/live/index.ts`, `server/src/ingest/ingest.ts` |
| Variant first-run onboarding: at build time and before each start (`refreshAuthEnv`), write `hasCompletedOnboarding: true` to `home/claude/.claude.json`; if it already exists, leave the file unchanged | `server/src/variants/index.ts` |
| API: `GET/POST /api/live`, `GET /api/live/:id`, `POST /api/live/resume`, `GET /api/live/resume-defaults`, `POST /api/live/:id/hook`, `POST /api/live/:id/driver`, `POST /api/live/:id/stop`, WebSocket `/api/live/:id/pty` (first sends the retained output; `{type:'input'}`, `{type:'resize'}`; for exited sessions, replays the last 4 MB of `pty.log`); SSE `live.updated`; Sessions list and detail return `liveId`; on service startup, running changes to exited (interrupted by service restart); on shutdown, all PTYs are ended | `server/src/api/live.ts`, `server/src/api/app.ts`, `server/src/api/sessions.ts`, `server/src/events.ts` |
| Page "Interaction": left list (running ones first), right tabs and xterm.js terminal (fit addon, fixed container height), variant, environment, working directory, replica repo and ticket, driver toggle, "Hand back to simulated user", "End process", resume when exited, expandable stage bars and request details (reusing `StageBars`, `RequestTimeline`), hints for starting / simulated user considers it finished / limit reached / error; new form (workflow, select task or on-the-spot input, "Save as task", variant on successful build, write hint for environment and real, initial driver); the "Interaction" marker and resume dialog in the Sessions list and detail; Tasks new page accepts `?mode=lfg&input=` and `?mode=ic-linear&issue=`; Vite proxy forwards WebSocket | `web/src/pages/live.tsx`, `web/src/components/live/`, `web/src/lib/live-api.ts`, `web/src/components/sessions/`, `web/src/pages/tasks-new.tsx`, `web/src/pages/tasks-import.tsx`, `web/vite.config.ts` |

## Key decisions

- Decided by the orchestrator (written into [[Contracts]] 14.2): isolated and real both pass `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, and hooks.json adds `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true`; isolated sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED=1` (Claude Code's own variable; the process runs in a sandbox and no longer asks whether to trust the directory); real's trust dialog is answered by a human; before the first `SessionStart` is received, the driver is fixed to human, and the page shows "Starting, confirmations in the terminal are answered by you"; the variant's config directory is marked as first-run onboarding completed by the dashboard, while "local config" is not written.
- Answer option menus by reading the screen before pressing keys (step 1, item 3): number keys and relative movement go wrong when a human has moved the cursor, when `↑` wraps around, or when the cursor is in the input box; read the cursor and checked state, then press keys step by step, waiting for the screen to change at each step; if more than 10 seconds pass, report an error with the screen contents.
- Driver switching is determined by hooks: do not answer when `Stop`'s `background_tasks` is non-empty (the same check as run's TurnTracker).
- Non-conforming WebSocket messages and input to an exited process: send the reason to this client as `{type:'error'}` and close this connection; the process and other connections are unaffected.
- The HOME for "local config" is `buildApp`'s `localHome` (defaults to the real HOME); tests use directories under `.work/`.
- isolated ic needs an ic task selected: the replica repo and replica ticket are both created from the task (section 13); a pasted ticket is first imported via "Save as task".

## Testing

Commands (repo root, `WFD_PORT=7330 WFD_WEB_PORT=5230`): `pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm e2e`. Everything uses real claude, real gateway, real GitHub and Linear.

- `server/test/live/keys.test.ts`: reads the menu from the real screens measured in step 1 (`test/fixtures/live/screens/`): the single-select cursor, the text already written under "other", the checked state of multi-select and the Next row; empty when what follows the tab bar is not this question.
- `server/test/live/live-restart.test.ts`: running interactions change to exited on service startup, with error "Interrupted by service restart"; already-exited ones are unchanged; `live.updated` is pushed.
- `server/test/live/live.test.ts` (baseline variant built for real):
  - real environment `/lfg build a calculator` in `.work/w30/real-cwd/` (empty directory after git init): process cwd (`lsof`), `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is the variant's config directory, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=<liveId>`, no `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED` (`ps eww`), argv starts with `claude`, no sandbox-exec; when the trust dialog appears, `starting` is true and the test answers it; no first-run onboarding.
  - The output received by two WebSocket clients is byte-identical and the screen is identical; the first message after disconnect and reconnect contains the startup screen and `/lfg build a calculator`; after resizing to 100 columns, Claude Code's horizontal line is 100 characters; after ending the process, status is exited, the exit code and exit event are recorded, and exited sessions replay pty.log.
  - resume: in this worktree, the session produced by `claude -p "Remember the passphrase: frog-47. Reply with just: Remembered"` (`test/fixtures/live/cfa31f10-….jsonl`), after import resumed with the baseline variant: copied to the variant's `projects/<liveId>/`, `sessions.file_path` points to it, `SessionStart.source` is resume, `transcript_path` is the copied file, waiting for the previous round's "Remembered"; after asking "What is the passphrase", `Stop.last_assistant_message` contains "frog-47"; original file sha unchanged, re-import raises no error. In the same session, have the agent call AskUserQuestion once (single-select, multi-select, single-select), `PreToolUse` recorded in `live_events`, `answerMenu` answers "Other: purple", "apple, orange, watermelon" (two items plus "Other"), "Shanghai"; the answers in the jsonl match these, then `Stop`.
  - "local config" resume (temporary HOME `.work/test-data/<pid>/home`): the process environment has no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `HOME` is a temp directory, session copied to `<HOME>/.claude/projects/<liveId>/`, argv has no variant `--model`.
- `server/test/live/live-simulated.test.ts` (isolated, `/lfg build a calculator`, initial driver is the simulated user): after receiving `SessionStart`, the driver becomes the simulated user (reason start); the simulated user answers the interview questions; the next time it waits for input, input comes from the client, the driver becomes human (reason input), and the answer being generated is discarded (`discarded: driver becomes human`); the human submits "For the following questions, please use AskUserQuestion... at least one multi-select question"; after release (reason release) the simulated user answers AskUserQuestion via keypresses, both single-select and multi-select. Runs from two `pnpm test` invocations (`.work/w30/live-simulated-summary.json`):

| Interactive | duration | agent cost | simulated user cost | AskUserQuestion answered by simulated user via keypresses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `l-20261011-d3e8re` | 1724 s | $7.51 | $0.10 | 2 times, 4 questions each; multi-select answer "one-click copy result, continue from last result" |
| `l-20261011-e5cgwx` | 359 s | $2.68 | $0.08 | 2 times (4 single-select; 1 single-select plus 2 multi-select), multi-select answer "order of operations and minus sign, exact calculation and display digits, Chinese error messages, auto-close right parenthesis" |

Both stopped the process after verification. This variant's interview also asks questions only in text (all four rounds of `l-20261011-a897cj` were text questions, simulated user answered in text), so the test has the human request AskUserQuestion.
- `e2e/live.spec.ts` (runs project, real build of variant): new form (link to save as task, write prompt for real), isolated `/lfg build a calculator` human-driven, Claude Code UI and initial message appear in the terminal, interview question appears; type text in the terminal and delete it; switch to the simulated user, simulated user answers; press ↓ to take over, driver becomes human; release; close page and reopen, process still running, terminal has content, the first message of another connection contains `/lfg build a calculator`; expand phase bar and request details; end process; in Sessions details, the "Interactive" marker and resume dialog (default this variant, recorded working directory, initial driver "human").
- `test/runs/simulated-user.test.ts` and `test/db.test.ts` updated to match the context shape and new tables.

Full check results: see next section.

## Merge with W31

The orchestrator first merged W31 (session binding to variant and analysis, [[Contracts]] section 15) into main `88445cb`; in `wfd-w30`, `git merge main`, merge commit `3f148e6`, no push, main not modified.

- Conflicts (13 files), both sides kept in all cases: `sessions` has `variant_id`, `variant_binding` and `live_id` at the same time; the Sessions API summary returns `liveId`, `variant`, `variantBinding` together, the list's workflow column shows the "Interactive" marker, the variant column shows the binding; events have both `analysis.updated` and `live.updated` (server types and the event list the page subscribes to); navigation has both "Interactive" and "Analysis", `e2e/home.spec.ts` checks Sessions, Runs, Interactive, Variants, Tasks, Compare in order, then Analysis; `api/app.ts` registers bindings and analysis first, then interactive; the gateway project in `vitest.config.ts` includes the live, insights and bindings tests.
- Migration: take the journal and `0006_snapshot.json` from main (`0006_session_variant_and_analyses`), delete this branch's `0006_live_sessions.sql`, and regenerate `0007_live_sessions.sql` on the merged schema (`live_events`, `live_sessions`, `sessions.live_id`, same content as before).
- Handoff:
  - Interactive sessions are bound to `live_sessions.variant_id` by calling W31's `bindLiveSession` after import (binding `run`); "Local config" is not bound. `LiveController` checks at startup and on each `session.updated`; a session is bound the first time it appears in `sessions`, and a new session swapped in by `/clear` is bound the same way (`server/src/live/controller.ts`).
  - The resume dialog's default variant reads `sessions.variant_id` (when unbound, it is Local config; when the bound variant is not a successfully built variant, the page likewise falls back to Local config) (`resumeDefaults` in `server/src/live/index.ts`).
  - Tests (`server/test/live/live.test.ts`): after an interactive session in the real environment is imported, `variant_id` is this variant, the binding is `run`, and `live_id` is this interaction; for a session imported from local, before resume the variant in `resume-defaults` is empty; after resuming with the baseline variant, the session is bound to it (binding `run`) and `resume-defaults` returns this variant; when resuming again with "Local config", the binding is not changed (`live_id` points to the new interaction, and the variant is still the previous one).
- The database in this branch's e2e data directory `.work/e2e/runs-data/` had the old `0006_live_sessions` applied before the merge, which conflicts with the renumbered migration (`table live_events already exists`). Delete that database; `prepare-runs-e2e.ts` rebuilds it and re-imports the four W4 runs. The user's `data/` was not changed. User instances and databases in other worktrees that applied the old `0006_live_sessions` will hit the same conflict; main's `data/db.sqlite` only applied main's migrations and is unaffected.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm typecheck`: passed. `pnpm lint`: 0 errors (the 1 warning is the existing `useVirtualizer`).
- `pnpm test`: web passed; of server's 299 cases, 298 passed. The 1 failure is W31's `insights-engines.test.ts` "Codex analyzes the same session", which timed out after 50 minutes; this branch did not change insights (`git diff main -- server/src/insights server/test/insights-engines.test.ts` is empty). All tests in `test/live/` and `bindings` passed.

## Open issues

- After a session is copied to another config directory and resumed, the original config directory still holds the old copy. Later, when the same session is resumed again in the original config, the copy already in the target config is not the same file as the one imported by the dashboard, so the error is reported unchanged (409) and nothing is selected automatically.
- isolated ic interactions require an ic task first; creating an isolated copy directly from a pasted ticket requires the import in section 13 (choosing repo and commit), and the form guides users to "Save as task".

# W34 interaction: resume, rename and importing local sessions

Tasks: see [[Task Board]]; contracts: see [[Contracts]] 14.1, 14.3, 14.5 (including the "Import into interaction area" section); requirements: see [[Requirements Log]] round 7, items 17 and 18, and the import requirements added afterward. Branch `wfd-w34`, based on main `450c923`, commits `75c1021` and `a74bc23`.

## What was done

| part | file |
|---|---|
| Data: one `live_sessions` item per Claude Code session (`claude_session_id` unique, add `title` and `updated_at`, drop process-related columns); new table `live_processes` (one row per start or resume); `live_events` adds `process_id`, and kind adds `resume`, `rename`, `import` | `server/src/db/schema.ts` |
| Migration `0009_live_items.sql`: old rows with the same `claude_session_id` are merged into one item, and each original row becomes one process (rows with an empty `resumed_from` are `start`, the rest are `resume`); when the session that `resumed_from` points to already has a row, the resumed row is merged into that item (including rows whose session id changed after /clear); an item takes its earliest row as representative; events and `sessions.live_id` point to the merged item, and the start event of a resume row is changed to resume; the name is the first 40 characters of the input or the session's title; `updated_at` is the maximum of the process start and end times | `server/drizzle/0009_live_items.sql` |
| Which item a resume lands on: if the session already belongs to an item, a `resume` process starts on that item; if it does not belong to any item yet, an item is created for it (named after its title in the Sessions list); if an item has a running process, 409; `resume-defaults` returns the item it belongs to and whether it is running; on the page, the resume button cannot be clicked while running | `server/src/live/index.ts`, `server/src/live/views.ts` |
| Terminal: `pty.log` is appended per item; each process writes a separator line when it starts (time, start or resume, variant); a new process's retained output starts from the last 4 MB of `pty.log`, and reconnecting replays this item's output | `server/src/live/pty.ts`, `server/src/api/live.ts` |
| Rename: `PATCH /api/live/:id { title }`; after trimming surrounding whitespace it must be non-empty and at most 200 characters, otherwise it errors (400); records a `rename` event (`{ from, to }`, `process_id` empty) and pushes `live.updated` and `session.updated`; the title in the Sessions list and details uses the item's name | `server/src/live/index.ts`, `server/src/api/sessions.ts` |
| Import into interaction area: `POST /api/live/import { sessionIds }`; checks all first (not found 404, already has an item 409 with a list, no recorded working directory 400), and creates items only if all pass; each item uses the `real` environment, with cwd set to the session's recorded cwd; no process is started, and an `import` event is recorded | `server/src/live/index.ts`, `server/src/api/live.ts` |
| Driver, status, exit code and error are now recorded on the process; hook and simulated-user events carry `process_id`; on service startup, running processes are changed to exited (interrupted by service restart) | `server/src/live/controller.ts` |
| Page: the left list shows name, status (running / exited / not running), variant, environment, and resume count; items with running processes come first, the rest sorted by `updated_at`; in the list and tabs, double-click or click the pencil icon to rename, Enter to save, Esc to cancel, and the server's original error text is shown on failure; above the list, an "Import local session" picker (search by title, directory, session id; multi-select; sessions already in the interactive area are labeled "already in interactive area" and cannot be selected); items that have never run show the session's conversation and resume button; after resume, the tab of this item is selected and the terminal reconnects to the process | `web/src/pages/live.tsx`, `web/src/components/live/live-title.tsx`, `web/src/components/live/import-sessions.tsx`, `web/src/components/live/resume-dialog.tsx`, `web/src/components/live/live-terminal.tsx`, `web/src/lib/live-api.ts` |

## Key decisions

- The migration runs in a drizzle transaction, and `PRAGMA foreign_keys` has no effect inside a transaction: first copy the old two tables to staging tables, clear `sessions.live_id`, then drop the old tables, rebuild them under their final names in parent-first order and write the data back, with foreign keys satisfied on every write; the test finally confirms with `pragma foreign_key_check`. The foreign keys from `live_processes` and `live_events` to items do not cascade on delete.
- When an item has no process yet (imported from local), `process` is empty, the status is `idle` (page shows "not running"), and the variant shows "—".
- The reconnect replay makes xterm.js answer the terminal queries in it (device attributes `ESC[?1;2c`, focus). These answers used to be written into the new process as input, echoed as `^[[?1;2c`, and when a simulated user was driving, they were also passed to the person as keypresses. Now the page sends no input until the replay has finished writing, and the e2e asserts that this text does not appear in the terminal after resume.
- When the process ends before the session is first imported (for example, it exits right after starting), the session used to not be bound to the variant used for this run; now, when the process exits, it is bound again after the last import.
- The e2e data directory `.work/e2e/runs-data/` is kept between runs and contains existing items and imported sessions: the test finds the items it created by id, and picks the session to import from sessions "not yet in the interactive area, with an existing working directory" (the run session imported by prepare-runs-e2e); when done, delete its `db.sqlite` so it is rebuilt. The W30 legacy data in this directory (`l-20261011-wefsob`) becomes one item with one process after migration 0009.

## Testing

Per the two tiers in _common.md: the basic tier runs in full; the real tier runs only the files covering this change. For real calls, choose the smallest cases that prove the behavior: newly created items end right after the initial message is submitted, resume asks only one question, and resume after import and resume from "local config" end right after startup.

### Basic tier

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`: passed (the 1 warning is the existing `useVirtualizer`).
- `vitest --project local`: 53 files, 258 cases all passed (157 seconds). On the first run, 6 cases in `github-pr`, `sessions-api`, `variants-api` timed out at 5 seconds; these three files were not changed, running them alone passed 16/16, and a full run again passed all. Added:
  - `test/live/live-migration.test.ts`: writes a database in the old structure (6 rows, two sessions resumed, one row with `resumed_from` pointing to an existing item but a different session id, 6 events, 4 sessions), and after migration asserts all fields of the two items, the items and kinds of the 6 processes, the items and processes of events, `sessions.live_id`, the foreign key check is empty, and `claude_session_id` is unique.
  - `test/live/live-import.test.ts`: after importing one short local session, the left list has one more item, with no process, status `idle`, the name is its title, one `import` event is recorded, and `resume-defaults` points to this item; a duplicate import returns 409 and lists it, a nonexistent one returns 404, an empty array returns 400, and none of them create an item.
  - `test/live/live-restart.test.ts`: for the same item, one process is exited first and the resumed process is still running; after the service starts, only the running one is changed to exited (interrupted by service restart).
- web vitest 6/6.
- e2e chromium, compare, environment projects: 24 passed, 3 failed. `sessions.spec.ts` rerun alone passed 2/2 (timed out when running in parallel with the other two projects). `tasks-import.spec.ts` (the acceptance criteria count 20 differs from the expected 8), `tasks.spec.ts` (rubric draft did not appear) call the real judge model; they are not part of the basic tier and are outside the scope of this change.

### Real tier (only files covering the changes are run)

| Test | Behavior proven | Duration | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `live.test.ts` create /lfg (real environment) | cwd, no sandbox, the variant's config directory, default name; both clients get identical output, reconnect first receives retained output, resize; session bound to variant | 13 seconds | $0 (ends right after the initial message is submitted; no completed model request) |
| `live.test.ts` rename | blank and 201-character names error with the original text, 200 characters allowed, `rename` event, Sessions list and detail show the new name, nonexistent returns 404 | no model call | — |
| `live.test.ts` interactive-area resume | still the same item, `live_processes` has start and resume; resume while running returns 409; reconnect replay contains two segments and a separator line; Claude Code answers "what did the previous message say" (including "calculator"); `pty.log` has two segments | 28 seconds | $0.085 |
| `live.test.ts` resume after import | the imported item has no process; after resume it is still this item, with a resume process | 1 second | $0 (ends right after startup) |
| `live.test.ts` Sessions first resume | a local session belonging to no item creates an item, named with its title; copied into the variant's `projects/<liveId>/`; answers "what is the passphrase" (frog-47); original file unchanged; one AskUserQuestion answered by keypresses for single choice, multiple choice and "Other" | 52 seconds | $0.221 |
| `live.test.ts` "local config" resume | still this item (resume 2 times); `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` not set, `HOME` is the test directory | does not wait for the model | $0 |
| `live-simulated.test.ts` | on the shortest single-round session: a simulated user answers a single-choice question by keypress; when a text question is asked, keypresses take over and the in-progress answer is discarded; after handing back, it continues answering | 38 seconds | agent $0.203, simulated user $0.013 |
| `e2e/live.spec.ts` (runs project) | new-item form; Claude Code appears in the terminal and accepts input; after resume the left item count is unchanged, the original tab is selected, resume 1 time, no `?1;2c`; double-click rename, Esc cancel, Enter save, blank name error; Sessions list and detail show the new name; import picker (sessions already in the interactive area cannot be selected) and resume after import | 27 seconds (plus 1.5 minutes for service startup) | $0 (all processes end before model requests complete) |

The two vitest files together took 222 seconds, with total cost about $0.52. In the real tier, `live.test.ts` and `live-simulated.test.ts` ran before the two fixes in `a74bc23` (rebinding once the process exits, and not sending input during page replay); these two fixes are covered by `e2e/live.spec.ts`, which ran afterward; the page fixes do not affect vitest clients that use WebSocket directly.

The user's `data/` was not changed. The tests created no GitHub objects: the real environment creates no repositories, gh write operations in vitest all error out (W32), and e2e uses only the real environment. The `wfe-l-20261012-ljhtgw`, `3ly3jc`, `7dbsez` newly added to txehq during this period come from the user's instance (these directories exist in `/Users/tester/orca/projects/wf-dashboard/data/live/`), not created by the tests.

## Open issues

- The session imported in e2e is the run session imported by prepare-runs-e2e, and the working directory it records is in the `wfd-w4` worktree. The resume after import starts claude in that directory and exits immediately without writing any file. After this worktree is deleted, this step has no usable session, and the test fails with the original error message, which indicates that the data directory must be rebuilt.
- The test fixture `11111111-…-000000000001.jsonl` records a working directory under `.work/` in the `wfd-w30` worktree, and the test creates this directory when it runs. After merging to main, the same absolute path is likewise created in the main checkout.
- The interactive area has no operation to delete an item yet, so items in the e2e data directory keep accumulating.
